title: India Women's Spinners Bundle Pakistan Out for 55 in Asia Cup Rout
excerpt: Left-arm spinner Shree Charani's 3 for 7 led a spin masterclass in Dubai, and Harmanpreet Kaur sealed a seven-wicket win in 8.4 overs in her 150th T20I as captain.
body:
• India bowled Pakistan out for 55 in 18.1 overs in Dubai — Pakistan's lowest total in women's T20I history.
  • Left-arm spinner Shree Charani (3/7) and leg-spinner Prema Rawat (3/9) led a spin masterclass that dismantled Pakistan.
  • India chased the target in 8.4 overs, winning by seven wickets with 68 balls to spare and topping Group A with six points.
  • Harmanpreet Kaur became the first captain, men or women, to lead a country in 150 T20Is; Shafali Verma became the youngest to 3,000 T20I runs.

The familiar spin choke

DUBAI: India's familiar spin choke returned at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday, as the Women in Blue bundled Pakistan out for 55 in 18.1 overs — their arch-rivals' lowest total in women's T20I history — and sealed a seven-wicket win in just 8.4 overs to top Group A of the Women's T20 Asia Cup with six points.

Pakistan won the toss and chose to bat, and openers Muneeba Ali (13) and Shawaal Zulfiqar (14) began confidently, reaching 27 without loss in a little over four overs. Then the spinners struck. Left-arm orthodox Shree Charani, the world's top-ranked T20I bowler, removed Gull Feroza and Zulfiqar in a single over; leg-break bowler Prema Rawat (3/9) and part-timer Shafali Verma (1/10) kept attacking the stumps with relentless accuracy; and Deepti Sharma (2/5) completed the formalities. No Pakistan batter beyond the openers reached double figures as the last ten wickets fell for 28 runs.

The chase was effectively over before it began. Shafali launched the very first ball over long-off for six, and although Pakistan captain Fatima Sana fought back with 3/17 — dismissing Shafali, Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana — Harmanpreet Kaur (18 not out) and Deepti Sharma (12 not out) steadied the innings. Harmanpreet fittingly finished it with a six down the ground.

Context & Background

It was India's fifth consecutive T20I victory over Pakistan across formats, and extended India's dominance in the Women's T20 Asia Cup, where the head-to-head now stands at seven wins to one. The victory completed a perfect group-stage campaign: India beat Thailand and Hong Kong before dispatching Pakistan.

The match carried extra weight for Harmanpreet Kaur, who became the first international captain — in men's or women's cricket — to lead her country in 150 T20Is. Shafali Verma's innings, though brief, carried her to 3,000 T20I runs at 22 years and 220 days, making her the youngest to reach the milestone and the fastest in terms of balls faced (2,182). Fatima Sana's 3/17 also made her just the fourth bowler from a full-member nation to take three wickets in a women's T20I powerplay twice in her career.

"I think Prema is superb, like natural talent she has. She has everything: fielding, batting, bowling — everything."

— Shree Charani, India spinner, on Prema Rawat

Diaspora Angle

The fixture remains appointment viewing for the South Asian diaspora, for whom India-Pakistan cricket transcends sport. This rout, delivered by a young spin attack in Dubai, gave fans across the United States, Canada, the UK and the Gulf a night to savour — and a new generation of heroes in Charani and Rawat.

What's Next

India head to the semifinals with an unbeaten record and a spin attack at full throttle. Pakistan, meanwhile, face a do-or-die final group clash against Hong Kong with a place in the final four at stake.

"It's simple, sir. One game at a time. It's not about anything."

— Shree Charani, on India's approach to the Pakistan game
